text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Norwegian universities put too much emphasis on examinations and too little on training and the practical needs of the job, according to a report by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD). However, overall the OECD's report is positive to the Norwegian system.

- Pilots and cabin staff at Braathens SAFE and Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) are protesting strongly against a new questionnaire from the Norwegian Aviation Authority asking personal details about an employee's health and sex life. All flight staff must answer the questionnaire in order to fly.

- Shipyards Kvaerner Rosenberg and Umoe Sterkoder will work with the navy and the Defence Research Institute to draw up the specifications for six new frigates. The project could be worth about six billion crowns to the two yards if they win the contract to build the ships. Kongsberg Gruppen is in the lead to supply equipment for the frigates.

- Norway's prawn industry, which is mainly based in Tromsoe in northern Norway, had pre-tax profits this year about the same as in 1996 at around nine million crowns on revenues of 500 million crowns. The industry has moved into the black after a crisis year in 1996.
